subject: Pilot affordability check — frozen budget & prioritized cost levers
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya@cardinalpay.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot affordability check — frozen budget & prioritized levers

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned while your budget team finalizes the Q4 spend window.

Key pain you described
- High per-transaction latency and growing token spend from multiple NLU passes in auth flows.
- Budget is currently frozen for new vendor spend until Q4; you need an evidence-backed phased approach to unblock incremental spend.
- Procurement requires a clear 30–60 day POC with a capped spend estimate and an escalation path to enterprise capacity if ROI is proven.

Goals we captured
1) Reduce token cost per auth session by ~25–40% without degrading accuracy.
2) Prove a predictable monthly run rate for 10k monthly auths in a 3-week POC window.
3) Deliver playbook for moving to Dedicated or Private deployment if model fidelity and unit-economics meet your targets.

Cost levers we discussed (short list)
- Batching: combine small concurrent requests (auth NLU + classification) into continuous batch windows — expected token-processing efficiency gain: ~20–30%.
- KV / prefix caching: cache stable prefixes and session KV across repeated patterns — incremental token reduction: ~10–15% on auth flows.
- Quantization profile: run lower-precision variant for high-volume paths; small accuracy hit but notable cost drop for background validation.
- Route fallbacks: route lower-priority calls to small, cheaper model variants in peak windows to cap spend.

Preliminary ROI anchors (ballpark) — see attached cost model for details
- Estimated baseline monthly token spend (current infra + volume): $14.2k
- With batching + caching in a conservative scenario: projected spend: $9.6k (~32% reduction).
- Two-phase POC stategy reduces upfront ask: Phase A scoped to most frequent auth path (expected sample size ~5k requests) with a $2.5k spend cap; Phase B expands once we validate quality/loss metrics.

Attachments I’m sharing
- pilot-scope-proposal.pdf (POC scope + success criteria)
- cardinalpay-cost-model-v1.xlsx (line-item token economics and sensitivity)
- redwood-batching-one-pager.pdf (technical approach in 1 page)

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) You loop in Procurement (procurement@cardinalpay.com) and confirm the $2.5k capped POC threshold & PO path.
2) We schedule a 30-minute kickoff next week to lock sample paths and logging hooks (needed for quality vs cost comparison).
3) Redwood provides a trimmed POC runbook and a 72-hour cost forecast once volume profile is shared.

If budget is still strictly frozen, we can tighten Phase A further to a 1k-sample smoke test (sub-$1k) to produce a quick fidelity-cost signal you can take to finance.

Thanks — available any time next week for the kickoff.

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 18:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot affordability check — frozen budget & prioritized levers

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:
- Budget note: Finance has a freeze on vendor spend until Oct; however, they are amenable to one-time proof-of-value spends under $3k that come with a clear expiration and success metrics.
- Procurement: looping in procurement but they’ll need a simple SOW and an explicit capped spend line.
- Scope request: please prioritize the single most expensive auth path (the step that hits external verification + 2 NLU calls). If you can show 25% cost reduction there we’ll have a stronger case for Q4.

Procurement (procurement@cardinalpay.com) — can you confirm the PO process for a one-time capped POC (<= $3k) and whether a short-term MSA addendum is needed?

Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Product | CardinalPay
alex@cardinalpay.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya@cardinalpay.com>, procurement@cardinalpay.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot affordability check — frozen budget & prioritized levers

Alex / team — great, good to know Finance will greenlight sub-$3k evidence spends. Quick response with a concrete, levered plan that fits your constraints:

Proposed two-phase, levered POC (trimmed to fit the spend cap)
- Phase A (7–14 days, capped $2.8k):
  - Scope: single auth path (external verification + 2 NLU calls) — we’ll instrument the same production traffic slice you described.
  - Levers: apply continuous batching + KV prefix caching + ephemeral quantized variant for background validation.
  - Success metrics: >=25% token spend reduction on scoped path; no more than 1% drop in end-to-end accuracy measured on your labeled holdout.
  - Deliverables: cost report, per-path token delta, recommended follow-up scope for Phase B, and our roll-to-dedicated checklist.

- Phase B (optional expand after success): larger volume (10k auths / month projection), Dedicated capacity walkthrough, and adjusted committed pricing options.

Anchor economics (conservative)
- Baseline modeled spend for scoped auth path (10k monthly equivalent): $4.8k
- Phase A projected (if levers applied and conservative adoption): $3.3k (~31% reduction)
- Key sensitivity: if session length or average tokens per auth exceed current sample by 20%, savings compress to ~18% — we’ll flag this in the runbook.

Docs attached: trimmed SOW statement at top of pilot-scope-proposal.pdf and a one-tab summary in cardinalpay-cost-model-v1.xlsx (tab: PhaseA-summary). I also attached the one-pager on batching for your architecture team.

If procurement confirms PO path, we can start onboarding by next Monday and have results within two weeks. Suggested kickoff times: Mon 10–11am PT or Tue 1–2pm PT — which works for you?

Thanks — will standby to draft the SOW and a short MSA addendum if procurement needs it.

—
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0133
